diet.text: Mainly toads and frogs; also fish

overview.text: The Barred Grass Snake is a harmless snake of western Europe that usually lives in or near water. It was counted as part of the Grass Snake until 2017, when DNA studies showed it is a separate species. It is the grass snake of Great Britain.

identification.text: Grey-green with black bars along the sides, a pale belly and a yellow-and-black collar behind the head.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Can grow to more than a metre long.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Great Britain (north to southern Scotland), the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, western Germany, France, Switzerland, Austria, Italy and northern Spain.

habitat.text: A strong swimmer often found near fresh water, especially pond edges, but also open woodland and the edges of fields and woods where it can bask.

diet.text: Mainly amphibians, especially common toads and common frogs, plus fish, small mammals and nestling birds. It searches actively for food, often at the water's edge.

reproduction.text: Mates in spring soon after coming out of hibernation. Females lay 8 to 40 leathery eggs in June or July, which hatch after about 10 weeks.

recognise.text: Black bars along the sides of a grey-green body.
